summary: Hand-check skip turns from the boards: was passing up the attack a mistake? Two independent readers per turn, then a synthesis

turns.legal_attack: Wondrous Waves (WWWW, 100) from Wailord ex 220/250 with 4 Water, decision 11: forecast expected_damage 70.0, ko_chance 1.0 against Castform Sunny Form 70/70 (1 Fire, Rocky Helmet).
turns.did_instead: Retreat:3 at d11, which swapped Wailord ex for the benched Wailord (B1 057, 200/200, energy []). With 0 Energy on the new Active the turn ended. km3_move = Attack:Wondrous Waves.
turns.facts: lib/card.py gives Wailord ex a retreat cost of 4, so the Retreat threw away all 4 Water. The decision log agrees: Wondrous Waves was not legal again until t16 (attaches @3 at t10, @3 at t12, @0 at t14, @0 at t16). Attacking would have scored a sure KO for 1 point (0-0 to 1-0) and removed the Castform, which Burns while our Soothing Shore (played at d9) is in play. Cost of attacking: 20 from Rocky Helmet. KO threat next turn if we attack: their benched Mega Blaziken ex (2 Fire) can Mega Burning for 120 plus Burn. Wailord ex would be at 200 after the Helmet and 220 after Soothing Shore's heal, so it survives; it was not in KO range. The Retreat brought no setup value: it put a 0-Energy body in front and cost four turns of attachments. The opponent later KO'd that Wailord (t13, 0-1). The deck still won 3-1.
turns.reason: The bot gave up a guaranteed KO (ko_chance 1.0) and kept none of its 4 attached Energy, for a Retreat that discarded all of them. Wailord ex was not in danger next turn, so nothing on the board pays for that.

turns.legal_attack: Sharp Fang (CC, 70) from Stoutland (A3a 056, 140/140, 2 Psychic), decision 31: forecast 70.0, ko_chance 0.0 against Baxcalibur 140/140.
turns.did_instead: EndTurn at d31, after Professor's Research, Watch Over x2 and Attach Psychic@0. km3_move = Attack:Sharp Fang.
turns.facts: The attack costs nothing: no discard, no recoil, and Baxcalibur has no Tool. It ends the turn exactly as EndTurn does. Their Active Baxcalibur has energy []. Buster Tail costs WWW, and Stoutland's Guard Dog Visage adds C while Stoutland is Active, so 4 in all. Zone plus Ice Maker gives at most 2 next turn, so Baxcalibur cannot attack. Its retreat of 3 can only be paid with an Inflatable Boat (making it 2). Seventy now plus 70 next turn is 140, a KO worth 1 point. The damage also makes it a Cyrus target (Cyrus is in our hand) if it does get out. Points 0-1, deck count 0. The deck won 3-1.
turns.reason: Attacking strictly beats EndTurn here: free damage against an Active that cannot hit back next turn, setting up an exact 140 KO.

turns.legal_attack: Sunny Scorching (R, 30; Burns the opponent's Active if a Stadium is in play) from Castform Sunny Form 70/70 with 1 Fire, decisions 5 and 7: forecast 30.0, ko_chance 0.0 against Heatmor (B1 044) 80/80.
turns.did_instead: Play:Field Blower at d5 (km3 proposed the same), then DiscardToolFromPokemon at d6 to remove their Rocky Helmet, then EndTurn at d7. km3_move at d7 = Attack:Sunny Scorching.
turns.facts: A Stadium was in play (DiscardActiveStadium was legal at d6), so the attack would also have Burned. The Helmet was already gone (theirs.active.tools [] at d7), so there was no recoil. Their Heatmor's Tongue Whip only hits the Bench (forecast 0 against our Active), so attacking changes no threat. That makes 30 damage plus Burn for free, but no KO. Low stakes: Mega Burning (120) KO'd the Heatmor at t5 anyway. Clearing the Helmet only makes sense if you then attack. The deck won 4-1.
turns.reason: The attack had no cost and was the follow-through on the Field Blower just played. Attacking weakly dominates EndTurn, though the stakes in this game were small.

turns.legal_attack: Tongue Whip (R; 30 damage to 1 of the opponent's Benched Pokémon) from Heatmor 10/80 with 1 Fire, legal at d9 and d10. The record's forecast (0.0, ko 0.0) is uninformative because it reads only their Active, which this attack cannot hit. By card text it KOs their benched Deino at 30/60 (with Deceptive Needle): 30 damage, and no Weakness on the Bench.
turns.did_instead: At d10, Retreat:2 (Heatmor to the Bench, discarding its Fire), then Play:Cyrus (pulled the 30-HP Deino into the Active) and Play:Rare Candy (Torchic in the Active to Mega Blaziken ex), then the turn ended. km3 proposed Attach@3 and then Attack:Tongue Whip at d10.
turns.facts: The attack meant a KO now for 1 point, and fewer Deino for their Hydreigon line. Next-turn threat: Bombirdier (1 Darkness) has Dark Cutter forecast at ko_chance 1.0 against our 10-HP Heatmor. Retreating did not save it: a damaged benched Heatmor stays a Cyrus target, and the opponent did take 1 point at t6 (Promote:0@3 at 0-1). Rare Candy could have gone onto the benched Torchic before attacking. So the line taken scored 0 and lost the Heatmor anyway; the attack line scores 1 and risks the same Heatmor. The deck won 4-2.
turns.reason: A sure 1-point KO on a benched Deino was available. The alternative scored nothing, and its only aim (saving the 10-HP Heatmor) failed against their Cyrus.

turns.legal_attack: Electrispark (L, 40; also 10 to each opponent's Benched Pokémon) from Heliolisk (B4 061) 60/80 with 1 Lightning, d26 and d27: forecast 40.0, ko_chance 0.0 against Butterfree (B3b) 120/130. Lightning Accelerator (110) was legal at d24-25 from Mega Manectric ex; km3 did not propose it.
turns.did_instead: Matched km3 exactly through d26: Evolve Heliolisk@3, Retreat:3 of the 50/210 Mega Manectric ex (retreat cost 0), Attach@2. Then EndTurn at d27, where km3_move = Attack:Electrispark.
turns.facts: Retreating the Mega was correct: Sunny Wind (60, ko_chance 1.0) on a 50-HP Mega ex would have given up 3 points and the game. After that, Electrispark costs nothing. The Heliolisk dies next turn either way (Sunny Wind 60 against 60 HP, ko 1.0), and it was KO'd at t12. Concrete threshold: Butterfree heals 20 when it uses Sunny Wind. With Electrispark it drops to 80, then heals to 100, which is inside Lightning Accelerator's 110 (80 + 30 × 1 point) at t13. Without it, Butterfree heals to 130, out of reach. At t13 the bot (and km3) indeed could not KO and retreated again. Caterpie on the Bench would also drop from 40 to 30. Points 1-0. The deck won 3-2.
turns.reason: A free 40 would have put Butterfree inside Mega Manectric ex's KO range for the next turn. The bot ended the turn with no attack instead.

turns.legal_attack: Peck (C, 10) from Natu (B1 097) 60/60 with 1 Psychic and Poison Barb, d5: forecast 10.0, ko_chance 0.0 against Suicune ex 160/160 (Giant Cape, 1 Water).
turns.did_instead: Evolve:Xatu@0 at d5. Xatu (A4 082, 80 HP) has only Life Drain, which costs PP, so with 1 Psychic no attack remained and the turn ended. km3_move = Attack:Peck.
turns.facts: Our Bench is empty (ours.bench []) and the hand holds no Basic, so a KO on our Active loses the game on the spot. Their Suicune ex needs one more Water to Crystal Waltz: 20 for each Benched Pokémon on both sides. That is 20 now (Frigibax) and 60 if they bench two more, exactly Natu's 60 HP. Xatu's 80 survives it. Evolving now costs no tempo: the Psychic stays through evolution, so Life Drain is ready at t5 either way (it was used at t5). Peck's 10 on a 160-HP ex is nearly worthless, because Life Drain sets the remaining HP to 10 regardless. Xatu survived t4. The game was lost 0-3 at t12 for other reasons.
turns.reason: Evolving buys 20 HP against a possible 60-damage Crystal Waltz while the bot has no Bench (a KO here loses the game). The 10 damage given up has almost no value next to Life Drain.

turns.legal_attack: Supernatural Feather (P, 50; discard a card from your hand, or the attack does nothing) from Oricorio (B4 078) 80/80 with 1 Psychic, legal d11-d16: forecast 50.0, ko_chance 0.0 against Vespiquen ex 120/170 (Leaf Cape, 1 Grass).
turns.did_instead: Matched km3 through d15 (Evolve Xatu@3, Place Natu@1, Professor's Research, Poké Ball, Attach@3), then EndTurn at d16, where km3_move = Attack:Supernatural Feather.
turns.facts: Hand at d16: Will, Copycat, Oricorio. Professor's Research was already played this turn, so neither Supporter (Will, Copycat) can be played now, and only one can be played next turn. Copycat is spare fuel for the discard. The Bench is full (3), so Oricorio can't be benched. Our Hiking Trail (played t2) is probably still in play (no Fragrant Forest UseStadium was offered), so the hand refills to 3 at end of turn and the discard costs about nothing. The 50 would put their only charged attacker, a 2-point ex, at 70; t-vespiquen has no healing. Two more Feathers then KO it instead of three, and the plan survives a Life Drain tails. Next-turn threat: Chase Order does 70, or 140 if they discard a Benched Basic Grass (Ogerpon ex or Shuckle ex). Our choice changes neither. Low stakes in this game: Will plus Life Drain set Vespiquen to 10 at t6 and Feather finished it at t8 (the deck won with the opponent out of Pokémon), so the 50 would not have changed the result.
turns.reason: Fifty permanent damage on their only attacker, for discarding a Supporter that couldn't be played this turn (and probably redrawn at end of turn). EndTurn gained nothing. The stakes were small in this game.

turns.legal_attack: Gnaw (W, 20) from Alolan Vulpix (B2 028) 60/60 with 1 Water, d5: forecast 40.0 (20 plus 20 Weakness; Castform is weak to Water), ko_chance 0.0 against Castform Sunny Form 70/70 with Rocky Helmet and energy [].
turns.did_instead: EndTurn at d5, after Poké Ball, Place Vulpix@3, Misty@3 (no Energy gained) and Attach@0. km3_move = Attack:Gnaw.
turns.facts: Attacking triggers Rocky Helmet (theirs.active.tools), doing 20 to our only charged Pokémon (60 to 40). Their Castform needs one attach to use Sunny Scorching (forecast 30), which also Burns (20 at Checkup) if a Stadium is in play; their list has Hiking Trail. Gnaw, Helmet, Scorching and Burn add up to 50 against a 40-HP Vulpix, so it could be KO'd before it evolves. Without Gnaw it ends at 10-30 HP. The 40 damage buys little: next turn Binding Snow (80 + 20 Weakness = 100) KOs a 70-HP Castform anyway, and it did at t4 (1-0). It would also KO a Torchic if Castform retreated. The deck won 4-2.
turns.reason: The attack's damage is not needed for next turn's KO, and its Rocky Helmet recoil can put the Vulpix in KO range before it evolves. Whether a Stadium was in play at t2 (not in the record) would settle how big that risk was; the verdict holds either way.

  - 09 Manectric: a free Electrispark would have put Butterfree inside next turn's KO range.

- **Mistakes with small stakes (2):**
